contract.goal: A deployable alerting-rules config in alerts.yaml (Prometheus rule format unless the person asks for another): symptom-level alerts, each with an expression, a non-zero for: duration, severity and routing labels, a summary and description, and a runbook link on page-level alerts, kept within the noise budget.

deliverables.description: The alerting-rules config, ready to deploy

criteria.text: alerts.yaml exists and holds real rule definitions, not a stub
Each alert has a metric expression (expr) and a for: duration
Alerts carry a severity label and a routing label such as team or service
Alerts are annotated with a summary and a description
Page-level alerts link to a runbook (runbook_url annotation)
No alert fires on a zero for: duration, so a passing spike never pages
The file parses as YAML and matches the target system's rule schema (groups[].rules[] for Prometheus)

judge.rubric: Does alerts.yaml parse as YAML and follow the target system's rule schema, with every alert complete (name, expr, for, labels, annotations)?

criteria.text: Every service or SLO the person named has at least one symptom-level alert (latency, errors, saturation, availability), with no unrequested, duplicate or overlapping rules

judge.rubric: Does every service or SLO the person named get at least one user-facing symptom alert, with no alerts nobody asked for and no two rules firing on the same condition?

criteria.text: Thresholds and for-durations match what was asked, and page-level alerts stay within the noise budget

judge.rubric: Do the thresholds and for-durations match the person’s targets, and does the number of page-severity alerts stay within the stated noise budget?
